title: The Silent Exam Hall
description:
An exam hall has a single row of N seats numbered 1..N. Students are paranoid about cheating accusations, so when a student arrives they always take the free seat whose distance to the nearest seated student is as large as possible. If several seats are equally good, they take the one with the smallest number. If the hall is empty, the student takes seat 1. Students may also leave at any time, freeing their seat.

You are given the log of Q events. Let sk be the seat taken by the k-th arrival (counting arrivals only, starting at 1). To keep the output short, print (1·s1 + 2·s2 + 3·s3 + ...) mod 1000000007.

In the example the first four arrivals take seats 1, 10, 5 and 3 (seats 3 and 7 are both at distance 2, and 3 is smaller). Then the student in seat 5 leaves, and the fifth arrival takes seat 6 (distance 3 to seat 3 and 4 to seat 10). The checksum is 1·1 + 2·10 + 3·5 + 4·3 + 5·6 = 78.

The hall can be enormous, so scanning the seats is hopeless; keep the gaps between seated students in a priority queue.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ N ≤ 109
  • 1 ≤ Q ≤ 105
  • Student ids are integers in [1, 109]. An A event never uses an id that is currently seated, and is never issued when all seats are taken. An L event always names a currently seated student. An id may arrive again after leaving.

Input

The first line contains N and Q. Each of the next Q lines is either A id (student id arrives) or L id (student id leaves).

Output

Print the checksum described above.

Example

Input:

10 6
A 1
A 2
A 3
A 4
L 3
A 5

Output:

78

title: Budget-Friendly Stretches
description:
A startup logged its daily profit (possibly negative) for n consecutive days. The investors call a stretch of consecutive days budget-friendly if the total profit over the stretch lies between L and R inclusive. Count the budget-friendly stretches.

Checking every stretch is far too slow for the full input. Think about prefix sums and a data structure that counts earlier prefix sums inside a value range.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 5·104
  • -109 ≤ profit ≤ 109
  • -1014 ≤ L ≤ R ≤ 1014

Input

The first line contains n, L and R. The second line contains the n daily profits.

Output

Print the number of pairs (i, j), i ≤ j, such that L ≤ ai + ... + aj ≤ R.

Example

Input:

5 -1 2
3 -2 1 -3 2

Output:

9
solution:
import sys
from bisect import bisect_left, bisect_right
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, L, R = int(d[0]), int(d[1]), int(d[2])
    P = [0] * (n + 1)
    s = 0
    for i in range(n):
        s += int(d[3 + i]); P[i + 1] = s
    vals = sorted(set(P)); m = len(vals)
    tree = [0] * (m + 1)
    ans = 0
    i = bisect_left(vals, 0) + 1
    while i <= m:
        tree[i] += 1; i += i & -i
    for j in range(1, n + 1):
        p = P[j]
        lo = bisect_left(vals, p - R); hi = bisect_right(vals, p - L)
        if hi > lo:
            c = 0
            i = hi
            while i > 0:
                c += tree[i]; i -= i & -i
            i = lo
            while i > 0:
                c -= tree[i]; i -= i & -i
            ans += c
        i = bisect_left(vals, p) + 1
        while i <= m:
            tree[i] += 1; i += i & -i
    print(ans)
main()

title: Rising Islands
description:
A volcanic sea is modelled as an R × C grid that is initially all water. Every day one cell rises above the sea and becomes land (a cell may be reported more than once — raising land again changes nothing). Two land cells belong to the same island if they share a side.

After each of the Q days the geologists record the number of islands. Report the sum of all recorded values and the largest recorded value. Recounting the islands from scratch every day is too slow.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ R, C ≤ 1000, R·C ≤ 106
  • 1 ≤ Q ≤ 105
  • 1 ≤ r ≤ R, 1 ≤ c ≤ C

Input

The first line contains R, C and Q. Each of the next Q lines contains a cell r c (1-based).

Output

Print two integers: the sum of the island counts after each day, and the maximum island count.

Example

Input:

3 3 5
1 1
1 3
3 3
1 2
2 3

Output:

9 3
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    R, C, Q = int(d[0]), int(d[1]), int(d[2])
    parent = [-1] * (R * C)
    cnt = 0; S = 0; M = 0; idx = 3
    for _ in range(Q):
        r = int(d[idx]) - 1; c = int(d[idx + 1]) - 1; idx += 2
        v = r * C + c
        if parent[v] == -1:
            parent[v] = v
            cnt += 1
            for nr, nc in ((r - 1, c), (r + 1, c), (r, c - 1), (r, c + 1)):
                if 0 <= nr < R and 0 <= nc < C:
                    u = nr * C + nc
                    if parent[u] != -1:
                        a = u
                        while parent[a] != a: a = parent[a]
                        while parent[u] != a: parent[u], u = a, parent[u]
                        b = v
                        while parent[b] != b: b = parent[b]
                        if a != b:
                            parent[a] = b
                            cnt -= 1
        S += cnt
        if cnt > M: M = cnt
    print(S, M)
main()

title: The Forgiving Manager
description:
A salesperson's daily results over n days are given (negative numbers are losses). For the yearly bonus the manager picks one stretch of consecutive days and, being forgiving, may additionally erase at most K days inside that stretch from the record. At least one day of the stretch must remain. The bonus equals the sum of the remaining days.

Find the largest possible bonus. Note that the answer may be negative if every day was a loss.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 5·104
  • 0 ≤ K ≤ 20
  • -109 ≤ ai ≤ 109

Input

The first line contains n and K. The second line contains the n daily results.

Output

Print the maximum bonus.

Example

Input:

7 1
3 -4 5 -1 -10 6 2

Output:

12
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, K = int(d[0]), int(d[1])
    a = list(map(int, d[2:2 + n]))
    NEG = -(1 << 62)
    g = [NEG] * (K + 1)
    best = NEG
    rng = range(1, K + 1)
    for x in a:
        v = g[0]
        ng = [(v if v > 0 else 0) + x]
        for j in rng:
            v = g[j]
            keep = (v if v > 0 else 0) + x
            dl = g[j - 1]
            ng.append(keep if keep > dl else dl)
        g = ng
        m = max(g)
        if m > best:
            best = m
    print(best)
main()

title: Conference Room Juggling
description:
A company has n meeting rooms numbered 0..n-1 and receives m meeting requests [s, e); all start times are distinct. Requests are handled in increasing order of their original start time:

  • If at time s some rooms are free (a room becomes free exactly at the end time of its last meeting), the meeting takes the free room with the smallest number.
  • Otherwise the meeting waits for the room that becomes free earliest (ties: smallest number) and then runs for its original duration e - s. Its delay is the waiting time.

Report the room that hosted the most meetings (ties: smallest number) and the total delay of all meetings.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 100
  • 1 ≤ m ≤ 105
  • 0 ≤ s < e ≤ 109, all s distinct

Input

The first line contains n and m. Each of the next m lines contains s e. Requests may be listed in any order.

Output

Print two integers: the busiest room and the total delay.

Example

Input:

2 4
0 10
1 5
2 7
3 4

Output:

0 10
solution:
import sys, heapq
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, m = int(d[0]), int(d[1])
    meet = sorted((int(d[2 + 2 * i]), int(d[3 + 2 * i])) for i in range(m))
    free = list(range(n)); heapq.heapify(free)
    busy = []
    cnt = [0] * n
    delay = 0
    for s, e in meet:
        while busy and busy[0][0] <= s:
            heapq.heappush(free, heapq.heappop(busy)[1])
        if free:
            rm = heapq.heappop(free)
            heapq.heappush(busy, (e, rm))
        else:
            t, rm = heapq.heappop(busy)
            delay += t - s
            heapq.heappush(busy, (t + e - s, rm))
        cnt[rm] += 1
    best = 0
    for i in range(1, n):
        if cnt[i] > cnt[best]:
            best = i
    print(best, delay)
main()

title: Skyline Renovation
description:
A street has n towers with heights h1, ..., hn. The mayor wants the skyline to be strictly increasing from left to right. Raising or lowering a tower by one metre costs one coin, and heights may become zero or even negative (basements count!). Find the minimum total cost.

A quadratic DP over candidate heights is too slow for n = 2·105. Hint: subtracting i from the i-th height turns “strictly increasing” into “non-decreasing”; then think about a max-heap (the classic slope trick).

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105
  • 1 ≤ hi ≤ 109
  • The answer can exceed 32-bit range.

Input

The first line contains n. The second line contains the n heights.

Output

Print the minimum cost.

Example

Input:

7
2 1 5 11 5 9 11

Output:

9
solution:
import sys, heapq
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n = int(d[0])
    h = []
    ans = 0
    for i in range(n):
        x = int(d[1 + i]) - i
        heapq.heappush(h, -x)
        top = -h[0]
        if top > x:
            ans += top - x
            heapq.heapreplace(h, -x)
    print(ans)
main()

title: Stone Duel
description:
Alice and Bob play with n stones in a row; stone i has value ai. Alice moves first and the players alternate. In one move a player removes either the leftmost or the rightmost remaining stone and scores points equal to the sum of the values of the stones that remain after the removal. The game ends when no stones are left.

Bob knows he will lose, so he plays to minimise the difference (Alice's score minus Bob's score), while Alice plays to maximise it. Print the difference under optimal play. Searching the game tree is exponential; memoise over the remaining interval, and keep the DP tight — there are about half a million intervals.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 1000
  • 1 ≤ ai ≤ 1000

Input

The first line contains n. The second line contains the n values.

Output

Print Alice's score minus Bob's score.

Example

Input:

5
5 3 1 4 2

Output:

6
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n = int(d[0]); a = list(map(int, d[1:1 + n]))
    P = [0] * (n + 1)
    for i in range(n):
        P[i + 1] = P[i] + a[i]
    dp = [0] * n
    for length in range(2, n + 1):
        nd = [0] * (n - length + 1)
        for l in range(n - length + 1):
            r = l + length - 1
            x = P[r + 1] - P[l + 1] - dp[l + 1]
            y = P[r] - P[l] - dp[l]
            nd[l] = x if x > y else y
        dp = nd
    print(dp[0])
main()

title: Graffiti on the Long Fence
description:
A fence consists of n planks numbered 1..n, all initially unpainted (colour 0). During the night q graffiti crews come one after another; crew j paints every plank from lj to rj with colour cj, covering whatever was there before.

In the morning the city wants to know how many different colours are visible on the fence (colour 0 does not count) and the checksum (1·col1 + 2·col2 + ... + n·coln) mod 1000000007. Repainting plank by plank costs up to n·q operations. Hint: process the crews in reverse — the last crew's colour is final, and each plank needs to be coloured only once if you can skip already-coloured planks quickly.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n, q ≤ 2·105
  • 1 ≤ lj ≤ rj ≤ n
  • 1 ≤ cj ≤ 109

Input

The first line contains n and q. Each of the next q lines contains l r c.

Output

Print two integers: the number of distinct visible colours and the checksum.

Example

Input:

6 3
1 4 5
3 6 2
2 2 5

Output:

2 51
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, q = int(d[0]), int(d[1])
    nxt = list(range(n + 2))
    col = [0] * (n + 2)
    for t in range(q - 1, -1, -1):
        b = 2 + 3 * t
        l = int(d[b]); r = int(d[b + 1]); c = int(d[b + 2])
        x = l
        while True:
            y = x
            while nxt[y] != y:
                y = nxt[y]
            while nxt[x] != y:
                nxt[x], x = y, nxt[x]
            x = y
            if x > r:
                break
            col[x] = c
            nxt[x] = x + 1
            x += 1
    colors = set(col[1:n + 1])
    colors.discard(0)
    M = 10 ** 9 + 7
    S = 0
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        S += i * col[i]
    print(len(colors), S % M)
main()

title: Compatible Server Pairs
description:
A data centre labels each of its n servers with a 20-bit configuration code. Two servers are compatible if the bitwise XOR of their codes is strictly less than a threshold K. Count the unordered pairs of distinct servers (by position; equal codes on different servers are different servers) that are compatible.

There are over a billion pairs in the largest input. Think about the highest bit where a XOR b first differs from K — a binary trie or bucketing by prefixes counts the pairs in O(n · 20).

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 5·104
  • 0 ≤ code < 220
  • 0 ≤ K ≤ 220

Input

The first line contains n and K. The second line contains the n codes.

Output

Print the number of compatible pairs.

Example

Input:

5 3
1 2 3 4 5

Output:

3
solution:
import sys
from collections import Counter
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, K = int(d[0]), int(d[1])
    a = list(map(int, d[2:2 + n]))
    total = 0
    for b in range(21):
        if (K >> b) & 1:
            t = (K >> b) ^ 1
            c = Counter([x >> b for x in a])
            if t == 0:
                total += sum(v * (v - 1) // 2 for v in c.values())
            else:
                g = c.get
                total += sum(v * g(p ^ t, 0) for p, v in c.items()) // 2
    print(total)
main()

title: The Amplifier Coupon
description:
A streamer's n consecutive videos earned a1, ..., an (negative values are losses). The platform offers a one-time amplifier coupon: choose at most one block of consecutive videos and multiply each of their earnings by the integer x (which may be zero or negative). Afterwards the streamer's highlight value is the maximum sum of a block of consecutive videos; the empty block is allowed, so it is never negative.

Maximise the highlight value. The two blocks (amplified and highlighted) may overlap arbitrarily. Trying every amplified block is cubic or at best quadratic; a DP with three phases (before / inside / after the amplified block) runs in linear time.

Constraints

  • 1 ≤ n ≤ 2·105
  • -100 ≤ x ≤ 100
  • -109 ≤ ai ≤ 109

Input

The first line contains n and x. The second line contains the n earnings.

Output

Print the maximum highlight value.

Example

Input:

5 -2
-3 8 -2 1 -6

Output:

22
solution:
import sys
def main():
    d = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n, x = int(d[0]), int(d[1])
    d0 = d1 = d2 = 0
    ans = 0
    for t in d[2:2 + n]:
        a = int(t)
        n0 = d0 + a
        if n0 < 0: n0 = 0
        n1 = (d0 if d0 > d1 else d1) + a * x
        if n1 < 0: n1 = 0
        n2 = (d1 if d1 > d2 else d2) + a
        if n2 < 0: n2 = 0
        d0, d1, d2 = n0, n1, n2
        if n1 > ans: ans = n1
        if n2 > ans: ans = n2
        if n0 > ans: ans = n0
    print(ans)
main()
